title: AI Receptionist Cost in 2026: Real Pricing, Hidden Fees and ROI for Small Businesses
subtitle: What you will actually pay per month, what the cheap plans leave out, and how to work out whether it pays for itself.
excerpt: Most small businesses pay $50–$400 a month for an AI receptionist in 2026. Entry plans start around $30 but usually include only 50–150 minutes; the real cost driver is call volume, overage per minute, and integrations. It pays for itself if it saves one missed job or booking a month.
metaTitle: AI Receptionist Cost 2026: Pricing, Hidden Fees & ROI
metaDescription: What an AI receptionist really costs in 2026: monthly price tiers, overage and setup fees, AI vs human comparison, and an ROI formula for small businesses.
metaKeywords: ai receptionist cost, ai receptionist pricing, ai receptionist for small business, virtual receptionist cost, ai answering service cost, ai phone answering
featuredImageAlt: AI receptionist answering a business phone call with a booking calendar
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
Short answer: in 2026 most small businesses pay $50–$400 per month for an AI receptionist. Entry plans are advertised from roughly $30, but they typically include only 50–150 minutes of calls. What you really pay depends on three things: how many minutes of calls you take, the per-minute overage rate once you pass your plan, and whether booking, CRM and calendar integrations cost extra.

This guide breaks down the price tiers, the fees that are easy to miss, how an AI receptionist compares with a human or a call-answering service, and a one-line formula to check the return before you sign anything. If you need the basics first, see what an AI receptionist is.

AI receptionist pricing tiers in 2026

Published pricing pages across the market cluster into three bands. The figures below are ranges compiled from vendor pricing pages in October 2026; check each vendor's current page before buying, because plans change often.

TierTypical monthly priceIncluded callsBest for
Starter$30 – $8050 – 150 minutesSolo trades, consultants, testing the idea
Professional$150 – $400300 – 1,000 minutesClinics, salons, home services, agencies
High volume / unlimited$500 – $800+Unlimited or very high capsMulti-location and busy front desks

A useful rule of thumb: an average business call lasts two to four minutes. A business taking 15 calls a day uses roughly 900–1,800 minutes a month, which already sits beyond most starter plans.

The fees that do not show up on the pricing page

  • Per-minute overage. Once you pass your plan, calls are commonly billed at roughly $0.25–$0.50 per minute. A busy week can double the bill.
  • Setup or onboarding. Some vendors charge a one-off fee to script the call flow, load your FAQs and connect your calendar.
  • Integrations. Booking into your calendar, logging leads in your CRM, or sending SMS follow-ups is sometimes locked to higher tiers.
  • Phone numbers and SMS. Extra local numbers, text-back messages and international calls may be billed separately.
  • Human handoff. Hybrid plans that route difficult calls to a live person cost noticeably more than AI-only plans.

AI receptionist vs human receptionist vs answering service

AI receptionistHuman receptionistCall answering service
Monthly cost$50 – $400 typicalFull salary plus benefitsUsually per-minute or per-call
Hours24/7, every dayBusiness hoursOften 24/7
Simultaneous callsMany at onceOneDepends on staffing
Books appointmentsYes, directly into your calendarYesOften takes a message only
Handles complex or emotional callsLimited, so it should hand offBestGood

The honest takeaway: an AI receptionist does not replace a great front-desk person for a premium in-person business. It replaces voicemail, the missed calls after hours, and the calls nobody can pick up while the team is busy. For most small businesses that is where the lost revenue is.

How to work out the ROI in one line

Monthly value = calls you currently miss per month × the share that would have booked × average job value.

Example: a plumbing business misses 40 calls a month. If even 10% would have booked a $250 job, that is $1,000 of recovered work against a $150–$300 subscription. You can check your own missed-call count in your phone provider's call log before you buy. That is real data, not a vendor estimate.

Related reading: why speed-to-lead matters and missed-call text-back, the cheapest automation to add alongside a receptionist.

What to check before you buy

  1. Listen to a real call. Ask for a live demo number and call it with your hardest question.
  2. Confirm the booking integration. It should write into the calendar you already use, not a separate one.
  3. Read the overage terms. Know the per-minute price and whether there is a monthly cap.
  4. Check the handoff. Urgent calls such as emergencies or complaints should transfer to a person or send an instant alert.
  5. Ask where recordings and transcripts are stored. This matters for regulated sectors; see HIPAA for healthcare.
  6. Start monthly. Avoid annual contracts until you have a month of call data.

When building your own makes sense

Off-the-shelf plans are the right choice for most small businesses. A custom AI voice agent makes sense when you need to look up live job or stock data, follow a regulated script, or connect to an in-house system that no vendor supports. ZetsApp offers both: the ready-to-use ZetDesk AI Receptionist, and custom AI automation when the standard product does not fit.

Frequently asked questions

How much does an AI receptionist cost per month?

Most small businesses pay between $50 and $400 a month in 2026. Starter plans begin around $30 but include few minutes, and high-volume or unlimited plans run $500–$800 or more.

Is an AI receptionist cheaper than a human receptionist?

Yes, by a wide margin on cost, and it answers 24/7 and handles several calls at once. A human is still better for complex, emotional or high-value in-person conversations, so many businesses use AI for overflow and after-hours calls.

Are there hidden costs with AI receptionists?

The common ones are per-minute overage once you exceed your plan, setup fees, paid integrations for calendars and CRMs, extra phone numbers or SMS, and higher prices for human-handoff plans.

Can an AI receptionist book appointments?

Yes. Good systems check live availability and book directly into your existing calendar or booking software, then send a confirmation by text or email.

How do I know if an AI receptionist is worth it?

Multiply the calls you miss each month by the share that would have become customers and by your average job value. If that number beats the subscription, it pays for itself.

title: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): How to Get Your Business Cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews
subtitle: A practical 2026 playbook for being the source AI answers quote, built on top of SEO rather than replacing it.
excerpt: GEO is the work of making your pages easy for AI answer engines to find, trust and quote. Start with solid SEO, then add answer-first passages, question-based headings, FAQ and Organization schema, an llms.txt file, crawler access for AI bots, fresh dates, and mentions of your brand on third-party sites.
metaTitle: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) Guide 2026
metaDescription: How to get cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews: a practical GEO checklist covering crawler access, answer-first content, schema and llms.txt.
metaKeywords: generative engine optimization, GEO, answer engine optimization, AEO, how to rank in ChatGPT, AI Overviews optimization, get cited by AI, llms.txt
featuredImageAlt: Search results and an AI answer panel citing a business website as its source
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the practice of making your content easy for AI answer engines (ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini and Google's AI Overviews) to find, trust and quote. Classic SEO earns you a blue link. GEO earns you a citation inside the answer.

The good news is that GEO is not a separate discipline. Every major AI engine still retrieves from a web index, so pages that cannot be crawled or ranked rarely get cited. GEO is SEO plus a set of habits that make each passage extractable. This is the checklist we apply to our own site and to client sites.

GEO vs SEO vs AEO: what is the difference?

SEOAEO (answer engine optimization)GEO
GoalRank a page in search resultsWin the direct answer (featured snippet, voice)Be quoted or cited in AI-generated answers
Unit that winsThe pageOne short answerA self-contained passage plus a trusted entity
Key signalsRelevance, links, technical healthDirect answers, question headings, FAQ schemaEverything on the left, plus clear entities, freshness and third-party mentions

Step 1: Make sure AI crawlers can actually read you

  • Allow the AI crawlers in robots.txt: GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot (OpenAI), ClaudeBot (Anthropic), PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended. Blocking them removes you from the candidate pool.
  • Serve real HTML. Many AI crawlers do not run JavaScript. If your site is a single-page app, pre-render or server-render it so the text is in the initial HTML. We had to do exactly this for our own Angular site.
  • Publish an llms.txt at your root: a plain-language summary of who you are and links to your most important pages.
  • Keep a clean sitemap with accurate lastmod dates.

Step 2: Write answer-first, extractable passages

AI engines lift passages, not pages. Write so that any single section still makes sense when it is quoted on its own.

  1. Put the answer in the first one or two sentences under each heading. Explain afterwards.
  2. Use the question as the heading. For example "How much does X cost?" rather than "Pricing considerations".
  3. Name things explicitly. Repeat the subject instead of writing "it" or "this tool", so a quoted sentence stays clear.
  4. Use tables for comparisons and numbered lists for steps. Both are easy to extract.
  5. Give specifics: ranges, thresholds, dates and named methods. Vague advice is rarely quoted.
  6. Add a TL;DR at the top of long articles.

Step 3: Add structured data that defines your entity

  • Organization schema with your name, logo, URL and sameAs links to your LinkedIn and other official profiles. This is how engines tie mentions back to you.
  • Article / BlogPosting with author, publish date and modified date.
  • FAQPage for genuine question-and-answer sections.
  • Product, Service and BreadcrumbList where they apply.

Structured data does not guarantee a citation, but it removes ambiguity about who said what and when.

Step 4: Earn information gain

An AI answer that already knows the generic facts has no reason to cite a page that repeats them. Pages that get quoted add something new:

  • Your own data, such as prices you charge, timelines you have delivered, or results you have measured.
  • A named framework or decision checklist.
  • A clear opinion on a trade-off ("choose A when…, choose B when…").
  • Practitioner detail that only someone who has done the work would know.

Never invent statistics to look authoritative. Unsupported numbers erode trust with readers and with the systems that rank you.

Step 5: Build third-party corroboration

AI engines lean on consensus. When several independent sources describe your business the same way, the model is more confident naming you. Practical sources:

  • Accurate, consistent listings on review platforms and business directories.
  • Guest articles and podcast appearances on sites in your niche.
  • Genuine answers on community sites where your buyers ask questions.
  • Partner and integration pages that link to you.

Step 6: Keep content fresh and measure it

  • Review your key pages every quarter and update facts, prices and the modified date. Only change the date when the content really changed.
  • Track AI referrals in analytics: traffic from chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai and similar domains.
  • Ask the engines your buyers' questions monthly and record whether you are cited and which page they quote.

A 30-day GEO starter plan

WeekFocus
1Crawler access, pre-rendering, sitemap, llms.txt, Organization schema
2Rewrite your top 10 pages answer-first with question headings and FAQ sections
3Publish two pages with genuine information gain: your pricing ranges, process or framework
4Directory and profile clean-up, two outreach placements, set up AI-referral tracking

If you would rather have it done for you, our team handles technical SEO, pre-rendering and content structure as part of website development, or as a standalone engagement. Tell us about your site.

Frequently asked questions

What is generative engine optimization?

Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the practice of structuring and publishing content so AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews can find it, trust it and cite it in their responses.

Is GEO replacing SEO?

No. AI engines retrieve from web indexes, so strong technical SEO and relevance remain the foundation. GEO adds extractable, answer-first writing, clear entity markup and third-party corroboration on top.

How do I get my website cited by ChatGPT?

Allow OpenAI's crawlers in robots.txt, make sure your text is in server-rendered HTML, answer questions directly under question-style headings, mark up your organization with schema, and earn mentions of your brand on other reputable sites.

What is llms.txt?

llms.txt is a plain-text file at the root of a website that summarises what the site is about and links to its most important pages, to help language models understand and navigate it. It is a proposed convention, not a ranking guarantee.

How long does GEO take to work?

Technical fixes can be picked up within weeks of the next crawl. Authority signals, such as third-party mentions and a history of being cited, build over months.

title: How Much Does It Cost to Build an AI Agent in 2026? Build, Run and Hidden Costs
subtitle: Realistic budget ranges by agent type, what drives the price, and the running costs most estimates leave out.
excerpt: A single-purpose AI agent with real integrations typically costs $15,000–$75,000 to build in 2026, a multi-step or multi-agent system $80,000–$250,000+, and a simple workflow automation can start under $10,000. Budget a further 15–30% of the build cost per year to run it: model usage, monitoring, evaluation and updates.
metaTitle: AI Agent Development Cost 2026: Build & Run Budget
metaDescription: AI agent development cost in 2026: build price ranges by complexity, what drives cost, monthly running costs and how to cut the budget without losing quality.
metaKeywords: ai agent development cost, cost to build an ai agent, ai agent pricing, custom ai agent development, agentic ai cost, llm app development cost
featuredImageAlt: Diagram of an AI agent connected to business tools, data sources and a human approval step
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
Short answer: in 2026 a single-purpose AI agent with real integrations typically costs $15,000–$75,000 to build. A multi-step or multi-agent system with compliance requirements costs $80,000–$250,000 or more. A simple LLM-powered workflow automation can start below $10,000. On top of the build, budget roughly 15–30% of the build cost per year to run and maintain it.

Published estimates vary wildly, from $10,000 to over $300,000, because "AI agent" covers everything from a chatbot that calls one API to an autonomous system acting across a dozen tools. Below is how we scope agents at ZetsApp, so you can place your own idea on the scale.

AI agent cost by complexity

TypeWhat it doesTypical build costTypical timeline
Workflow automationOne LLM step inside a fixed flow, for example classify an email and draft a reply$3,000 – $10,0001 – 3 weeks
Single-purpose agentChooses between several tools to finish one job, for example a support agent that looks up orders and issues refunds under a limit$15,000 – $75,0004 – 10 weeks
Multi-step / multi-agent systemPlans, delegates to specialised agents, works across many systems, keeps memory$80,000 – $250,000+3 – 6 months
Regulated enterprise agentAny of the above with audit trails, data residency and formal evaluation, for example in finance or healthcareAdd 25 – 60%Add 1 – 3 months

These are planning ranges, not quotes. The fastest way to a reliable number is a short discovery phase that fixes scope, integrations and success criteria.

What drives the price

  1. Number and quality of integrations. Each system the agent touches needs authentication, error handling and tests. A clean REST API is cheap; a legacy system with no API is not. Standards such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) reduce this cost when your tools support it.
  2. Autonomy level. An agent that only drafts actions for a human to approve is far cheaper to make safe than one that acts on its own.
  3. Knowledge grounding. If the agent must answer from your documents, you need a RAG pipeline: ingestion, chunking, a vector index and retrieval tuning.
  4. Evaluation. Production agents need a test set of real cases and automated scoring. Skipping this is the most common reason pilots never reach production.
  5. Security and compliance. Permission scoping, prompt-injection defences, PII handling, audit logs, and regulatory requirements such as GDPR or the EU AI Act.
  6. Interface. Running inside Slack, Teams, WhatsApp or your existing app is usually cheaper than building a new front end.

The running costs most estimates leave out

Cost lineWhat it coversTypical range
Model usageLLM API tokens. Agents call the model several times per task$50 – $5,000+ per month, depending on volume and model
Hosting and dataServers, vector database, queues, logs$50 – $1,000 per month
Monitoring and evaluationTracing, quality dashboards, regression tests when models changeA few hours to a few days per month
MaintenanceTool and API changes, new edge cases, prompt and model upgradesOften 15 – 30% of build cost per year

Model usage is the line that surprises people. Estimate it early: tasks per day × model calls per task × tokens per call × price per token. Then design to reduce it, for example by routing simple steps to a smaller, cheaper model.

How to reduce the cost without reducing quality

  • Start with a human in the loop. Ship the agent as an assistant that proposes actions, and remove approvals step by step as accuracy is proven.
  • Automate one workflow end to end before building a general-purpose agent.
  • Use existing platforms for chat, voice and messaging channels instead of building them.
  • Mix models. Use a frontier model only where reasoning is hard, and smaller models for classification and extraction.
  • Define success numerically before writing code, for example "resolves 60% of tier-1 tickets with under 2% wrong refunds".

Build, buy or both?

Buy when a mature product already does the job, such as an AI receptionist or a website chatbot. Build when the agent must work inside your own systems, rules and data, which is where it creates an advantage competitors cannot buy. Many businesses do both: they buy the channel and build the logic behind it. For the architectural choice between agents, RAG and fine-tuning, see our decision framework.

ZetsApp scopes and builds production agents with a fixed-scope quote after a short discovery phase. See our AI development services.

Frequently asked questions

How much does it cost to build a simple AI agent?

A simple LLM-powered workflow automation typically costs $3,000–$10,000, and a single-purpose agent that uses several tools with proper integrations and testing typically costs $15,000–$75,000 in 2026.

What does it cost to run an AI agent each month?

Running costs are mainly model API usage, hosting and monitoring. They range from under $100 a month for low-volume internal tools to several thousand dollars for high-volume customer-facing agents. Plan roughly 15–30% of the build cost per year for maintenance.

How long does it take to build an AI agent?

A focused workflow automation takes one to three weeks, a single-purpose agent four to ten weeks, and a multi-agent enterprise system three to six months or more.

Why do so many AI agent pilots fail to reach production?

The usual causes are unclear success criteria, no evaluation set, too much autonomy too early, and underestimated integration and security work. Starting with a human-approved assistant and measuring accuracy avoids most of them.

Is it cheaper to use an off-the-shelf AI agent?

For common jobs such as phone answering, website chat and scheduling, yes. Custom agents are worth it when the work depends on your own systems, data and rules.

title: What Is MCP (Model Context Protocol)? A Plain-English Guide for Businesses in 2026
subtitle: How MCP connects AI assistants to your tools and data, what it changes for integration cost, and the security rules to set before you switch it on.
excerpt: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard, introduced by Anthropic in November 2024 and since adopted by OpenAI, Google and Microsoft tools, that lets AI assistants connect to business tools and data through one common interface. Build one MCP server for a system and any compatible AI app can use it, which cuts integration work, provided you scope permissions carefully.
metaTitle: What Is MCP (Model Context Protocol)? Business Guide
metaDescription: MCP explained in plain English: how the Model Context Protocol connects AI assistants to business tools and data, use cases, costs and security rules.
metaKeywords: what is mcp, model context protocol, mcp server, mcp for business, mcp explained, ai integrations, ai agents tools
featuredImageAlt: AI assistant connected through MCP servers to a CRM, database and document store
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to your business tools and data through one common interface. Anthropic introduced it in November 2024, and OpenAI, Google and Microsoft have since added support across their AI products. Instead of building a custom integration for every AI app and every system, you build one MCP server for a system, and any MCP-compatible AI client can use it.

A good analogy is USB-C for AI. Before USB-C every device needed its own cable; before MCP, every AI-to-tool connection needed its own custom code.

How MCP works in three parts

PartWhat it isExample
MCP host / clientThe AI application the user talks toClaude, ChatGPT, an IDE assistant, or your own in-house agent
MCP serverA small service that exposes one system's capabilities in the MCP formatA server for your CRM, your database or your document store
CapabilitiesWhat the server offers to the AITools (actions such as "create invoice"), resources (data such as "customer record"), prompts (reusable templates)

When a user asks "what did Acme order last quarter, and draft a renewal quote", the AI client discovers which tools the connected servers offer, calls the CRM server to read the orders, then calls the quoting tool, all through the same protocol.

Why MCP matters for businesses

  • Lower integration cost. One server per system, reused by every AI app, instead of N apps × M systems custom connectors.
  • Less lock-in. You can switch AI providers or models without rebuilding your integrations.
  • A growing catalogue. Many SaaS vendors now publish official MCP servers, so common tools may already be covered.
  • A single control point. Access, logging and rate limits live in the server, which is easier to govern than prompts scattered across apps.

Practical use cases

  1. Internal knowledge assistant: answers from wikis, policies and tickets, with links back to the source.
  2. Sales assistant: reads the CRM, summarises accounts, drafts follow-ups and logs activity.
  3. Operations and maintenance: queries asset and work-order systems, for example "which pumps are overdue for preventive maintenance?"
  4. Finance back office: pulls invoices, flags anomalies and prepares reconciliations for human approval.
  5. Developer productivity: connects coding assistants to repositories, issue trackers and logs.

The security rules to set before switching it on

MCP makes it easy to give an AI real power over real systems, which is exactly why you should be deliberate about it.

  • Least privilege. Give each server the narrowest permissions it needs, and start read-only.
  • Act as the user, not as an admin. Use the end user's own credentials or scoped tokens so the AI cannot see more than the person asking.
  • Human approval for writes. Require confirmation for actions that send, pay, delete or change records.
  • Treat tool output as untrusted. Content fetched from emails, web pages or documents can contain prompt-injection instructions. The client must never execute them blindly.
  • Only install servers you trust. Third-party MCP servers run code with access to your data; review them like any other dependency.
  • Log everything. Every tool call should be recorded with who, what and when.

What it costs to adopt MCP

If an official MCP server already exists for your tool, the cost is mainly configuration, permission design and testing, often days rather than weeks. A custom MCP server for an in-house system is a small, focused development project, typically a few days to a few weeks depending on how many actions it exposes and how clean the underlying API is. That is usually less than building separate integrations for each AI app. For whole-agent budgets, see what it costs to build an AI agent.

How to get started

  1. List the three questions or tasks your team would most like an AI assistant to handle.
  2. Map which systems hold the data or actions for each one.
  3. Check whether official MCP servers exist for those systems.
  4. Pilot with read-only access and a small group of users.
  5. Add write actions with human approval once accuracy is proven.

ZetsApp builds custom MCP servers and agents that connect AI to line-of-business systems such as ERP, CMMS and CRM. See our AI development services or book a scoping call.

Frequently asked questions

What is MCP in AI?

MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard that defines how AI applications connect to external tools and data sources, so one integration can be reused by any compatible AI assistant.

Who created the Model Context Protocol?

Anthropic introduced MCP as an open standard in November 2024. It has since been adopted by other major AI providers and many software vendors.

What is an MCP server?

An MCP server is a small service that exposes a system's actions (tools), data (resources) and templates (prompts) in the MCP format, so AI clients can discover and use them.

Is MCP secure?

MCP is a protocol; security depends on how you deploy it. Use least-privilege permissions, user-scoped credentials, human approval for write actions, trusted servers only, and full logging of tool calls.

Do I need MCP to build an AI agent?

No, but it reduces integration work and lock-in when an agent needs several tools or when multiple AI apps need the same systems.

title: How to Choose CMMS Software in 2026: A Practical Checklist for Maintenance Teams
subtitle: The features that actually reduce downtime, the questions to ask vendors, and how to roll it out so technicians use it.
excerpt: Choose a CMMS on five things: preventive maintenance scheduled by calendar AND meter or run-hours, a mobile app technicians can use offline, an asset register with history, spare-parts tracking tied to work orders, and reports on PM compliance, MTTR and MTBF. Run a trial with your own technicians before you sign.
metaTitle: How to Choose CMMS Software 2026: Buyer Checklist
metaDescription: CMMS buying guide for 2026: must-have features, calendar and run-hours PM scheduling, offline mobile use, pricing models, KPIs and a rollout plan.
metaKeywords: how to choose cmms software, cmms software, best cmms for small business, preventive maintenance software, maintenance management software, cmms checklist
featuredImageAlt: Maintenance technician using a CMMS work order app on a tablet next to industrial equipment
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
Short answer: choose a CMMS (computerised maintenance management system) on five things:

  1. Preventive maintenance scheduled by both calendar and meter readings (run-hours, cycles or output).
  2. A mobile app technicians can use offline.
  3. A clean asset register with full history.
  4. Spare-parts inventory linked to work orders.
  5. Reporting on PM compliance, MTTR and MTBF.

Everything else is secondary. Then run a two-to-four-week trial with your own technicians before you sign.

New to the term? Start with what a CMMS is and how it differs from an EAM.

Signs you have outgrown spreadsheets

  • Preventive tasks are missed because nobody saw the reminder.
  • The same breakdown happens again and nobody can find what was done last time.
  • Technicians wait for parts that were "definitely in stock".
  • You cannot answer "how much did this machine cost us in maintenance last year?"
  • Audits mean days of chasing paper work orders and signatures.

The must-have feature checklist

FeatureWhy it mattersWhat to test in the trial
Preventive maintenance schedulingPrevents the breakdowns that cause most unplanned downtimeCreate a task due every 30 days or 500 run-hours, whichever comes first
Work ordersThe core record of what was done, by whom, with which partsRaise, assign, complete and close a job from a phone in under two minutes
Mobile and offlinePlant rooms, ships and basements often have no signalComplete a job in airplane mode, then sync
Asset hierarchy and historyFind every past job on a machine in secondsImport 20 of your real assets with parent/child structure
Spare parts and inventoryStops waiting for parts and over-stockingConsume a part on a work order and watch stock and reorder alerts update
Meter readingsEnables usage-based and condition-based maintenanceEnter a run-hours reading and see the next due date move
Reporting and KPIsProves the system works and guides budgetRun PM compliance, MTTR and MTBF for a test period
Permissions and audit trailNeeded for ISO, safety and regulatory auditsCheck who changed what, and when

The KPIs your CMMS must report

  • PM compliance: the share of scheduled preventive tasks completed on time. This is the first number to improve.
  • MTTR (mean time to repair): how long it takes to restore equipment after a failure.
  • MTBF (mean time between failures): how long equipment runs between failures. It should rise as preventive maintenance improves.
  • Planned vs unplanned work ratio: more planned work means fewer emergencies.
  • Maintenance cost per asset: the basis for repair-or-replace decisions.
  • For production lines, connect maintenance data to OEE.

How CMMS pricing works

ModelHow it is chargedWatch out for
Per user per monthEach named technician or planner pays a seat feeRead-only and requester users charged as full seats
Per asset or sitePrice scales with equipment count or locationsCosts jump when you add a site
Tiered plansFeatures unlocked by plan levelPreventive maintenance, inventory or the API locked to top tiers
One-off licence or custom buildUpfront cost, then supportWho maintains it, and how upgrades work

Ask every vendor for the total yearly cost for your real user count, asset count and sites, including implementation, data import and training. Comparing headline seat prices is misleading.

Questions to ask every vendor

  1. Can preventive tasks trigger on run-hours or meter readings, not just dates?
  2. Does the mobile app work fully offline, including photos and signatures?
  3. Will you import our existing asset list and maintenance history, and at what cost?
  4. Is there an API, and is it included in our plan?
  5. Where is our data hosted, and can we export all of it if we leave?
  6. What does onboarding include, and how long until technicians are live?

A rollout plan technicians will actually use

  1. Start with critical assets only. Take the 20% of equipment that causes 80% of downtime, rather than everything at once.
  2. Load preventive tasks from manufacturer manuals and your team's own experience.
  3. Train on phones, on the floor, with real jobs, not in a classroom.
  4. Make the CMMS the only way to request work. No more side-channel requests.
  5. Review PM compliance weekly for the first three months.

Off-the-shelf or custom?

Most small and mid-sized teams should start with an off-the-shelf CMMS. A tailored system is worth it when you need maintenance tied to your ERP, regulatory regimes such as class-society or safety-management rules, offline-first operation in remote locations, or multi-site fleets with unusual asset structures. ZetsApp offers ZetMaint CMMS with calendar and run-hours scheduling and an offline technician app, and builds custom maintenance platforms for complex operations.

Frequently asked questions

What should I look for in CMMS software?

Prioritise preventive maintenance scheduling by calendar and meter readings, a mobile app that works offline, an asset register with full history, spare-parts tracking linked to work orders, and reporting on PM compliance, MTTR and MTBF.

What is the difference between CMMS and EAM?

A CMMS focuses on maintenance execution: work orders, preventive maintenance, parts and technicians. An EAM covers the full asset lifecycle, including procurement, financial depreciation and disposal, and is usually larger and costlier.

How much does CMMS software cost?

Pricing is usually per user per month, per asset or site, or by plan tier. Compare the total yearly cost for your real users, assets and sites, including implementation, data import and training, rather than headline seat prices.

How long does it take to implement a CMMS?

A small team that starts with its critical assets can be live in a few weeks. Larger multi-site rollouts with data migration and integrations typically take two to six months.

Do small businesses need a CMMS?

If you maintain equipment whose failure stops revenue and you are tracking maintenance on paper or spreadsheets, a CMMS usually pays back through fewer breakdowns, faster repairs and less wasted inventory.

title: Website Security Headers Checklist 2026: CSP, HSTS, Permissions-Policy and the Rollout Order That Won't Break Your Site
subtitle: The eight response headers every business website should send, what each one blocks, and copy-paste configs for Nginx, Apache, IIS, Vercel and Cloudflare.
excerpt: Eight HTTP response headers block most browser-side attacks: Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options (or frame-ancestors), X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy. Roll them out in order of risk, ship CSP in report-only mode first, and re-scan after every deploy.
metaTitle: Website Security Headers Checklist 2026 (CSP, HSTS)
metaDescription: The 8 security headers every website needs in 2026, what each blocks, safe rollout order, and copy-paste configs for Nginx, Apache, IIS, Vercel and Cloudflare.
metaKeywords: security headers checklist, http security headers, content security policy example, hsts header, permissions policy header, x-frame-options, website security best practices 2026
featuredImageAlt: Checklist of HTTP security headers next to a website security grade
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
Security headers are instructions your server sends with every page that tell the browser what it may and may not do: only connect over HTTPS, only run scripts from approved origins, never let another site frame the page, and so on. They cost nothing, need no code changes, and close the gaps most automated scanners and security questionnaires look for first.

This is the checklist we use on client sites and on our own Angular site, including the mistakes we made rolling it out. Run your domain through the free ZetsApp Website Security Audit before and after, so you can see the grade move.

The 8 security headers at a glance

HeaderBlocksRecommended valueRisk of breaking the site
Strict-Transport-SecurityHTTPS downgrade and cookie theft on public Wi-Fimax-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preloadLow, once every subdomain has HTTPS
Content-Security-PolicyCross-site scripting (XSS), data exfiltration, rogue third-party scriptsSite-specific allow-listHigh: test in report-only first
X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestorsClickjackingSAMEORIGIN and frame-ancestors 'self'Low, unless partners embed you
X-Content-Type-OptionsMIME sniffing (uploads executed as script)nosniffVery low
Referrer-PolicyLeaking full URLs (tokens, search terms) to other sitesstrict-origin-when-cross-originVery low
Permissions-PolicyEmbedded frames requesting camera, microphone, location, paymentcamera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()Low: allow features you actually use
Cross-Origin-Opener-PolicyCross-window attacks and XS-Leakssame-origin-allow-popupsLow; plain same-origin can break OAuth and payment pop-ups
Cross-Origin-Resource-PolicyOther sites embedding your files (Spectre-style leaks)same-siteMedium if other domains hotlink your images

You can drop X-XSS-Protection. Modern browsers removed the filter it controlled, and the old filter could itself be abused. If you still send it, set it to 0.

The rollout order that won't break production

  1. Day 1, zero-risk headers: X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Permissions-Policy. Deploy, re-scan, done.
  2. Day 1, HSTS with a short max-age: start at max-age=86400, confirm every subdomain serves HTTPS, then raise it to two years and add includeSubDomains; preload. Preloading is hard to undo, so only submit to hstspreload.org when you are sure.
  3. Week 1, CSP in report-only: send Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only with your best-guess policy and read the violations in the browser console (or collect them with report-to). Add each legitimate origin you find.
  4. Week 2, enforce CSP: switch the header name to Content-Security-Policy. Keep the report-only header alongside it with a stricter draft for the next iteration.
  5. Then COOP and CORP: check that sign-in pop-ups (Google, Microsoft, Stripe, PayPal) still work.

Writing a Content-Security-Policy that survives real life

CSP is the header with the most protection and the most breakage. A practical starting policy for a marketing or SaaS site:

default-src 'self';
script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net;
style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com;
font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com;
img-src 'self' data: https:;
connect-src 'self' https://api.yourdomain.com;
frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com;
object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self';
frame-ancestors 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests

Four lessons from hardening our own site:

  • Inventory before you write. We grepped the codebase and our CMS content for every external host. The surprise was not the CDN scripts we knew about but a browser-side call to an AI API buried in one tool, plus scripts loaded on demand by two components.
  • Same-origin iframes inherit the parent's CSP. Blog posts we render inside srcdoc/document.write iframes run inline scripts. A policy without 'unsafe-inline' silently broke every one of them, even though the iframe looked separate. Either move that content to its own origin or accept 'unsafe-inline' for now and plan the migration.
  • A hash or nonce disables 'unsafe-inline'. If you add 'sha256-…' for one inline snippet, browsers ignore 'unsafe-inline' for everything else. Go all-in on hashes or nonces, or do not use them at all.
  • Remove eval() instead of allowing it. A calculator on our site used eval on user input. Replacing it with a 120-line whitelist parser let us drop 'unsafe-eval' and closed a self-XSS hole at the same time.

Copy-paste configs by platform

Nginx

add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;
add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
add_header Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()" always;

The always flag matters: without it Nginx omits the headers on 4xx and 5xx responses.

Apache (.htaccess, mod_headers)

Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
Header always set X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN"
Header always set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

Vercel (vercel.json)

{ "headers": [ { "source": "/(.*)", "headers": [
  { "key": "X-Content-Type-Options", "value": "nosniff" },
  { "key": "X-Frame-Options", "value": "SAMEORIGIN" } ] } ] }

On Vercel, vercel.json must sit in the root of the deployed folder. If you upload a pre-built dist folder, a vercel.json in the project root is ignored. This exact mistake kept our own headers from going live for weeks.

IIS / ASP.NET Core

Add headers in middleware with context.Response.OnStarting, call app.UseHsts() outside development, set AddServerHeader = false on Kestrel, and remove X-Powered-By in web.config under httpProtocol/customHeaders.

Headers are half the job: cookies, DNS and email

  • Cookies: session cookies need Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax. A missing Secure flag on an HTTPS site counts as a failure in most audits.
  • SPF and DMARC: without an enforced DMARC policy (p=quarantine or p=reject) anyone can send phishing that appears to come from your domain. Our audit flags this on most small-business sites we scan.
  • security.txt: publish /.well-known/security.txt with a contact address and expiry date (RFC 9116). Note that some static-site build tools skip dot-folders when copying, so check that the file is actually deployed.
  • Subresource Integrity: pin versioned CDN scripts with integrity="sha384-…" so a compromised CDN cannot inject code.

How to verify

Run the ZetsApp Website Security Audit after each step. It reads your live headers, certificate, cookies and DNS, grades the site A+ to F, and generates the missing headers for Nginx, Apache, IIS, Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare in one block. It also produces a branded PDF you can attach to a client handover or a vendor security questionnaire.

If you would rather have it done for you, our cloud and DevOps team hardens headers, TLS and email authentication, usually within a day. Ask for a hardening quote.

Frequently asked questions

What are the most important HTTP security headers?

Strict-Transport-Security (forces HTTPS), Content-Security-Policy (limits which scripts can run), X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors (stops clickjacking) and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are quick wins on top.

Do security headers affect SEO?

Not directly as a ranking factor, but HTTPS is a confirmed signal, and headers like HSTS and a working CSP protect against injected spam links and malware that can get a site flagged or deindexed.

Will a Content-Security-Policy break my website?

It can, if it omits an origin your pages use. Deploy it first as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, fix every legitimate violation, and only then switch to the enforcing header.

Is X-XSS-Protection still needed?

No. Browsers removed the XSS auditor it controlled. Set it to 0 or remove it, and rely on a Content-Security-Policy instead.

How do I check my website's security headers?

Use a scanner such as the free ZetsApp Website Security Audit, which reads your live headers and grades them, or open your browser developer tools, select the page request in the Network tab and read the response headers.

title: OWASP Top 10:2025 Explained: What Changed, What It Means for Your Web App, and What to Fix First
subtitle: Security Misconfiguration jumps to #2, Software Supply Chain Failures arrive at #3, SSRF is folded into Broken Access Control, and a new category covers how apps fail under stress.
excerpt: The OWASP Top 10:2025 keeps Broken Access Control at #1 (now including SSRF), moves Security Misconfiguration to #2, adds Software Supply Chain Failures at #3 and introduces Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions at #10. For most teams, the fastest wins are configuration hardening, dependency hygiene and server-side authorization checks.
metaTitle: OWASP Top 10 2025: What Changed and What to Fix
metaDescription: OWASP Top 10:2025 explained: new categories, what moved, and a fix-first plan for access control, misconfiguration and supply-chain risk.
metaKeywords: owasp top 10 2025, owasp top 10 changes, software supply chain failures, security misconfiguration, broken access control, mishandling of exceptional conditions, web application security
featuredImageAlt: OWASP Top 10 2025 categories listed from broken access control to exceptional conditions
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
The OWASP Top 10 is the most widely used list of critical web application security risks, and the reference point for most security questionnaires, penetration-test reports and compliance checklists. The 2025 edition is the first update since 2021. It reflects two shifts: attackers going after configuration and dependencies rather than code alone, and applications that fail in unsafe ways when something unexpected happens.

The OWASP Top 10:2025 list

#2025 categoryChange from 2021
A01Broken Access ControlStill #1, now also covers Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
A02Security MisconfigurationUp from #5
A03Software Supply Chain FailuresNew: expands "Vulnerable and Outdated Components"
A04Cryptographic FailuresDown from #2
A05InjectionDown from #3 (includes XSS)
A06Insecure DesignDown from #4
A07Authentication FailuresRenamed from "Identification and Authentication Failures"
A08Software or Data Integrity FailuresSame position
A09Security Logging and Alerting FailuresRenamed to stress alerting, not just logging
A10Mishandling of Exceptional ConditionsNew category

Always check the official list at owasp.org for the final wording and the mapped CWEs. This article focuses on what the changes mean in practice.

What actually changed, and why it matters

Security Misconfiguration moved to #2

Modern apps are mostly configuration: cloud storage permissions, CDN rules, CORS, response headers, debug flags, default admin panels. One wrong setting exposes more than one bad line of code. This is also the cheapest category to fix. Missing HSTS, an absent Content-Security-Policy, permissive CORS and verbose error pages all show up in a five-minute scan. Run your production domain through the free ZetsApp Website Security Audit to see your browser-facing configuration graded in seconds.

Software Supply Chain Failures is a new #3

The 2021 list warned about outdated components. 2025 widens that to the whole chain: package registries, build pipelines, CI secrets, CDN-hosted scripts and the AI coding assistants that suggest dependencies. Practical controls:

  • Lock files committed and enforced (npm ci, not npm install, in CI).
  • Automated dependency alerts (Dependabot, Renovate, npm audit, dotnet list package --vulnerable).
  • Subresource Integrity hashes on every versioned CDN script.
  • A software bill of materials (SBOM) generated at build time.
  • Verifying that packages an AI assistant suggests actually exist and are the real ones. "Slopsquatting" attackers register package names that models commonly hallucinate.

SSRF folded into Broken Access Control

Server-side request forgery, where an attacker makes your server fetch an internal URL such as a cloud metadata endpoint, is now treated as an access-control failure. That is the right framing: the server is acting on a resource the user should never reach. If your app fetches user-supplied URLs (link previews, webhooks, importers, "scan my site" tools), resolve the host yourself and refuse private, loopback, link-local and metadata IP ranges at connect time, not only when you parse the URL. Otherwise DNS rebinding gets around the check.

Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions is new at #10

This category covers apps that do not prevent, detect or respond correctly to unusual situations: unhandled exceptions that leak stack traces, logic that fails open (a permission check that returns "allowed" when the policy service times out), partial transactions left half-applied, and resource exhaustion. The fix is mostly discipline: fail closed, use global exception handlers that return generic messages, wrap multi-step writes in transactions, and set timeouts and size limits on every external call.

A fix-first plan for small and mid-size teams

  1. This week, configuration (A02): security headers, TLS, cookie flags, CORS allow-list, disable directory listing and debug output. Mostly one-line changes.
  2. This month, access control (A01): make sure every API endpoint checks that this user may act on this record (no IDOR), deny by default, and add tests for it.
  3. This month, supply chain (A03): turn on dependency alerts, pin and hash CDN scripts, and lock down CI secrets.
  4. This quarter, alerting and exceptions (A09, A10): alert on repeated auth failures and 5xx spikes, and review the code paths that fail open.

How OWASP maps to compliance

ISO 27001 auditors, SOC 2 assessors and PCI DSS 4.0 (requirement 6) all expect you to address the OWASP Top 10 or an equivalent. Showing a recent scan, a dependency policy and an access-control test suite covers most of the evidence they ask for.

Frequently asked questions

What is new in the OWASP Top 10 2025?

Two new categories (A03 Software Supply Chain Failures and A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions), Security Misconfiguration rising to #2, SSRF merged into A01 Broken Access Control, and A09 renamed to Security Logging and Alerting Failures.

What is the number one OWASP risk in 2025?

Broken Access Control: users being able to view or change data or functions they should not, now including server-side request forgery.

Is XSS still in the OWASP Top 10?

Yes. Cross-site scripting is part of A05 Injection. A strict Content-Security-Policy and framework output encoding are the main defences.

How do I test my website against the OWASP Top 10?

Combine an automated configuration scan (such as the ZetsApp Website Security Audit) for misconfiguration and supply-chain signals with dependency scanning in CI and a manual penetration test for access control and business logic.

title: Google AI Mode SEO in 2026: How to Earn Inline Links and Citations (Updated for the October Changes)

excerpt: Google AI Mode now shows inline links inside answers more often and is testing a block of official-site links for tasks that rely on one or two sources. metaDescription: How to get cited and linked inside Google AI Mode answers in 2026, updated for October's inline-link and official-site changes.

featuredImageAlt: Google AI Mode answer with inline source links pointing to a business website
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
Google AI Mode is Google's conversational search experience, the full-page version of the AI Overviews that appear above regular results. Google said at I/O 2026 that it had passed a billion monthly users, and in October 2026 it announced changes to how it links out. If your traffic from informational queries has been flat or falling, this is where those clicks are going.

What changed in October 2026

  • Inline links are more common. Google says links placed on the words inside an AI Mode response now appear much more often, and that these get higher engagement than links listed beside the answer.
  • An "official sites" block is being tested. For tasks that depend on one or two official sources (renewing a licence, a company's own pricing or support page), Google is testing a block of official-site links above the AI answer.
  • Timely news carousels are expanding to more countries and languages.

Google has also said plainly that optimising for AI search is SEO. Its guidance does not require llms.txt or "chunking" as separate steps. Treat any vendor selling a separate "AI Mode ranking factor" with caution.

SEO vs AEO vs GEO in AI Mode

What winsWhat you do
SEO (retrieval)Being in the index and relevant for the fan-out sub-queries AI Mode runsCrawlable HTML, fast pages, clean canonicals, topical clusters, links
AEO (the answer)A passage that answers one sub-question completelyQuestion headings, answer in the first two sentences, tables and steps
GEO (the citation)Being the source the model trusts enough to link inlineClear entity data, original information, corroboration on other sites

For the full GEO playbook see our generative engine optimization guide. Below are the AI Mode-specific moves.

1. Win the fan-out, not just the head query

AI Mode breaks a question into many related sub-queries and pulls passages for each. A page that ranks for "best CMMS software" but has nothing on cost, implementation time or mobile use loses those sub-answers to someone else. Map the 8–15 follow-up questions a buyer would ask and answer each one under its own heading. Answer pages like our question-per-page library exist for exactly this.

2. Write passages worth an inline link

Inline links attach to specific claims. The passages that earn them share four traits:

  1. A specific, checkable statement: a number, threshold, date, named method or price range, not a generality.
  2. Self-contained: it still makes sense quoted alone, so name the subject instead of writing "it".
  3. Original: your own data, test, framework or practitioner detail. Google's 2026 updates favour information gain; a paraphrase of the top results has nothing to cite.
  4. Easy to extract: short paragraphs, comparison tables, numbered steps.

3. Claim the "official site" slot for your own brand tasks

If Google is testing an official-sites block for single-source tasks, make it unmistakable that your domain is the official source for your brand, products and support:

  • Organization schema with url, logo and sameAs links to your verified profiles.
  • Dedicated, crawlable pages for pricing, support, contact, documentation and status. Do not bury them in PDFs or JavaScript-only widgets.
  • Consistent naming across your site, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn and directories.

4. Make sure Google can actually render you

Single-page apps still lose here. We found our own Angular site served the homepage shell, with the homepage canonical, on hundreds of article URLs until we prerendered them. Check with "View source", not DevTools: if the answer text is not in the raw HTML, plenty of AI crawlers will never see it.

5. Trust signals still gate citations

Author pages with real credentials, visible publish and update dates, references to primary sources, and a secure site (HTTPS, no malware, no injected spam) all feed the trust judgement. You can check the security side in seconds with our free website security audit, and the content side with the E-E-A-T signal checker.

How to measure AI Mode visibility

Search Console reports AI Mode and AI Overview clicks and impressions inside the normal Performance report rather than as a separate filter, so watch impressions on question-style queries alongside click-through rate. Supplement that with manual checks of your 20 most valuable questions each month, noting whether you are cited inline, in the side panel or not at all.

Frequently asked questions

How do I rank in Google AI Mode?

Rank in normal search first, because AI Mode retrieves from Google's index. Then answer the related sub-questions a searcher would ask, each in a self-contained, specific passage, mark up your organization and content with schema, and publish original information worth citing.

Is AI Mode SEO different from regular SEO?

Google says optimising for AI search is still SEO. The emphasis shifts toward passage-level answers, covering follow-up questions and being a trusted, clearly identified source.

Do I need llms.txt for Google AI Mode?

No. Google's guidance does not require llms.txt. It can still help other AI tools understand your site, but it is not a Google ranking requirement.

What are inline links in AI Mode?

Links placed on specific words or claims inside the AI-generated answer, pointing to the source page that supports that claim. Google reported in October 2026 that they now appear much more often and get higher engagement.

Can I track AI Mode traffic in Search Console?

AI Mode clicks and impressions are counted within the standard Search Console Performance report. Track question-style queries and supplement with manual spot checks.

title: EU AI Act Update (October 2026): What the Digital Omnibus Delay Changes for Your AI Product, and What It Doesn't
subtitle: High-risk deadlines moved to December 2027 and August 2028. Prohibited practices, general-purpose AI rules and most transparency duties did not move.
excerpt: Under the Digital Omnibus agreement, obligations for stand-alone high-risk AI systems (Annex III) move to 2 December 2027 and for AI embedded in regulated products (Annex I) to 2 August 2028. Prohibited practices (since February 2025) and general-purpose AI model duties (since August 2025) are unchanged, and the Article 50 transparency duties largely keep their original schedule.
metaTitle: EU AI Act Delay 2026: New Deadlines Explained
metaDescription: EU AI Act Digital Omnibus explained: new high-risk deadlines (Dec 2027 / Aug 2028), what did not move, and a 90-day compliance plan.
metaKeywords: eu ai act delay, digital omnibus ai act, eu ai act high risk deadline 2027, eu ai act article 50 transparency, eu ai act compliance checklist, ai act gpai obligations
featuredImageAlt: Timeline of EU AI Act obligations showing the postponed high-risk deadlines
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
This is a practical engineering summary, not legal advice. Confirm the dates against the amended regulation as published in the Official Journal of the EU, and involve counsel for your specific use case.

The EU AI Act applies in phases. In 2026 the EU agreed a "Digital Omnibus" package that postpones the obligations for high-risk AI systems, which many companies had been racing to meet by August 2026. Lawmakers reached a provisional agreement on 7 May 2026, Parliament voted to adopt it on 16 June 2026, and law-firm reports say the Council gave final approval at the end of June.

The EU AI Act timeline after the Digital Omnibus

ObligationApplies fromChanged?
Prohibited AI practices (social scoring, manipulative AI, most real-time remote biometric ID, emotion recognition at work and school)2 February 2025No
AI literacy duty for providers and deployers2 February 2025No
General-purpose AI (GPAI) model obligations2 August 2025No
Transparency duties (Article 50): tell people they are talking to AI, label deepfakes, mark AI-generated contentLargely 2 August 2026, with a short grace period reported for marking content from systems already on the marketMostly no
Stand-alone high-risk systems (Annex III: hiring, credit scoring, education, essential services…)2 December 2027Yes, postponed
High-risk AI embedded in regulated products (Annex I: medical devices, machinery, toys…)2 August 2028Yes, postponed

What this means if you build or sell AI software

If you ship a chatbot, voice agent or AI assistant

You are most likely limited-risk, and Article 50 is what applies to you, on roughly the original schedule. In practice:

  • Tell users they are interacting with an AI system unless it is obvious from context. For voice agents, say it at the start of the call.
  • Mark synthetic audio, images, video and text in a machine-readable way where your system generates them (watermarks or metadata such as C2PA content credentials).
  • Label deepfakes and AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest.

Our ZetVoice AI agent and ZetDesk AI receptionist announce themselves as AI by default for exactly this reason.

If your AI makes decisions about people

Hiring, credit, insurance pricing, education access and benefits eligibility are Annex III use cases. You have until December 2027, but the work is substantial: a risk-management system, data governance, technical documentation, logging, human oversight, accuracy and robustness testing, a quality-management system, and registration in the EU database. Teams that start in 2027 will not finish in time.

If you fine-tune or build on a foundation model

GPAI obligations already apply to model providers. If you substantially modify a model and place it on the market under your own name, you may take on provider duties for that modification. Keep records of training data sources, compute and evaluation.

A 90-day plan that is useful whatever the final dates

  1. Inventory: list every AI feature, the model and vendor behind it, what data it uses, and who it affects.
  2. Classify: prohibited, high-risk (Annex I or III), limited-risk (Article 50) or minimal. Write down the reasoning.
  3. Close the transparency gaps now: AI disclosures in the UI, content marking and updated privacy notices. Our free AI disclaimer generator drafts the statement.
  4. Log and monitor: keep inputs, outputs, model versions and human overrides for high-impact decisions. This is also what GDPR Article 22 reviews will ask for.
  5. Secure the system: the Act's robustness and cybersecurity requirements overlap heavily with the OWASP Top 10 and basic hardening. Start with a website security audit of every public endpoint.

How the AI Act interacts with GDPR

The AI Act does not replace GDPR. If your AI system processes personal data you still need a lawful basis, a DPIA for high-risk processing, data-subject rights and processor agreements with AI vendors. Our GDPR-compliant AI development checklist covers that side.

ZetsApp designs AI products with compliance built in, including logging, human-in-the-loop review and EU-region hosting. See our AI development services or talk to an engineer.

Frequently asked questions

Has the EU AI Act been delayed?

Partly. The Digital Omnibus postpones high-risk obligations: stand-alone Annex III systems to 2 December 2027 and AI in regulated products (Annex I) to 2 August 2028. Prohibitions, AI literacy and general-purpose AI model duties already apply and were not delayed.

Do chatbots need to comply with the EU AI Act in 2026?

Yes, through the Article 50 transparency duties, which largely keep their original schedule: users must be told they are interacting with AI, and AI-generated content must be marked where applicable.

What counts as a high-risk AI system?

Systems listed in Annex III, such as AI used in hiring, credit scoring, education, essential public and private services, law enforcement and migration, plus AI that is a safety component of products covered by EU product law (Annex I).

What are the fines under the EU AI Act?

Up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for prohibited practices, and lower tiers for other breaches. The Omnibus also eases some requirements for smaller companies, so check the final text.

title: Passkeys for Business Websites in 2026: How They Work, What They Cost to Add, and How to Roll Them Out Without Locking Users Out
subtitle: Passwordless sign-in with Face ID, fingerprint or a device PIN is now supported by every major browser and password manager. Here is the implementation plan we use.
excerpt: Passkeys replace passwords with a cryptographic key pair stored in the user's phone, laptop or password manager and unlocked with Face ID, fingerprint or PIN. They are phishing-resistant, cannot be reused or leaked from your database, and are supported by all major platforms. Add them alongside existing sign-in first, offer them after login, and keep a tested recovery path.
metaTitle: Passkeys for Business Websites: 2026 Rollout Guide
metaDescription: How passkeys work, why they stop phishing, what they cost to add to your website or SaaS, and a rollout plan that avoids lockouts.
metaKeywords: passkeys, passkey implementation, passwordless login, webauthn tutorial, fido2 passkeys website, add passkeys to website, passkey vs password
featuredImageAlt: User signing in to a business website with a passkey and fingerprint prompt
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
A passkey is a sign-in credential that replaces a password with a public/private key pair. The private key stays on the user's device or in their password manager (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, Microsoft, 1Password, Bitwarden and others) and is unlocked with Face ID, a fingerprint or the device PIN. Your server stores only the public key, so there is nothing worth stealing and nothing a phishing page can capture.

Passkeys vs passwords vs one-time codes

PasswordPassword + SMS/app codePasskey
Phishing-resistantNoNo: codes can be relayed in real timeYes: bound to your domain
Database breach exposes loginHashes can be crackedPartlyNo: only public keys stored
Reuse across sitesCommonCommonImpossible
User effortType and rememberType plus wait for codeOne biometric tap
Running costReset emails, supportSMS feesNone per sign-in

How passkeys work, in one paragraph

At registration the browser asks the user's authenticator to create a key pair for your domain (the relying party ID) and sends you the public key. At sign-in your server sends a random challenge. The authenticator signs it with the private key after the user unlocks it, and your server checks the signature with the stored public key. Because the key is tied to your exact domain, a look-alike phishing site cannot request it. This is the WebAuthn / FIDO2 standard every major browser implements.

The rollout plan

  1. Add passkeys alongside existing sign-in. Do not remove passwords on day one.
  2. Offer creation after a successful login ("Sign in faster next time with Face ID?"). Conversion is far higher than on a cold settings page.
  3. Enable autofill sign-in (conditional UI): add autocomplete="username webauthn" to the username field so saved passkeys appear in the browser's autofill list.
  4. Allow several passkeys per account and show where each was created, so users can add a second device and remove a lost one.
  5. Design account recovery before launch. Recovery is where attackers go once the front door is strong. Use a verified email plus a second factor, or support-assisted recovery with identity checks. Never a single SMS.
  6. Measure passkey adoption, sign-in success rate and recovery requests. Only then consider making passkeys the default for new accounts.

Libraries that do the hard part

  • Node.js: SimpleWebAuthn (server and browser packages).
  • .NET: the Fido2 .NET library (Fido2NetLib), or the passkey support being added to ASP.NET Core Identity.
  • Python: py_webauthn.
  • Hosted: most identity platforms (Auth0, Clerk, Microsoft Entra, AWS Cognito, Firebase via extensions) now offer passkeys as a setting.

Never write the signature-verification code yourself. Use a maintained library and keep it updated. That is supply-chain hygiene from the OWASP Top 10:2025.

What it costs

On a hosted identity platform, passkeys are usually a configuration change plus UI work: a few days. On a custom auth stack, budget roughly 1–3 weeks of engineering for registration, sign-in, conditional UI, device management, recovery and tests. There are no per-authentication fees, and support costs for password resets go down.

Passkeys don't fix everything

Passkeys secure the sign-in step. Session cookies still need Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite, your site still needs HTTPS with HSTS, and your APIs still need server-side authorization on every request. Check the browser-facing parts with our free website security audit.

ZetsApp adds passkeys and modern authentication to existing products as part of our web app development work. Ask for an estimate.

Frequently asked questions

Are passkeys more secure than passwords?

Yes. Passkeys cannot be phished, reused or leaked from a server breach, because the private key never leaves the user's authenticator and only works on the domain it was created for.

What happens if a user loses their phone?

Synced passkeys are restored from the user's password manager or platform account on a new device. For device-bound passkeys, users need a second registered passkey or your account-recovery process, so design recovery before launch.

Do passkeys work on all browsers?

All current major browsers and operating systems support passkeys through WebAuthn, including Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox on desktop and mobile.

Can I use passkeys and passwords together?

Yes, and you should at first. Offer passkeys as an option, encourage adoption after login, and keep passwords or another fallback until most active users have a passkey.

title: Vibe-Coding Security: The 12 Risks Hiding in AI-Generated Apps (and a Checklist to Catch Them Before Launch)
subtitle: AI coding tools ship working features fast, and the same predictable security holes along with them. Here is what to review before real users and real data arrive.
excerpt: AI-generated apps tend to fail security in predictable ways: secrets in client code, missing server-side authorization, disabled database row-level security, permissive CORS, unvalidated input, hallucinated or outdated packages and no rate limiting. A one-day review against a checklist, plus an automated configuration scan, catches most of them before launch.
metaTitle: Vibe Coding Security Risks: 12-Point Checklist
metaDescription: The 12 most common security holes in AI-generated (vibe-coded) apps and a pre-launch checklist to find and fix them.
metaKeywords: vibe coding security, ai generated code security risks, security review ai code, lovable bolt cursor security, supabase rls security, slopsquatting, secure ai coding checklist
featuredImageAlt: AI coding assistant generating an app with security warnings highlighted
author: ZetsApp Engineering
content:
Vibe coding means describing what you want to an AI tool and accepting the code it produces, often without reading it line by line. It has made shipping a working prototype a matter of hours. The catch is that "working" and "safe" are different tests, and AI tools optimise for the first. The good news is that the security mistakes are repetitive, so a checklist catches most of them.

The 12 most common security holes in AI-generated apps

#RiskWhat it looks likeFix
1Secrets in the clientAPI keys for OpenAI, Stripe or a database admin key bundled into front-end JavaScriptMove calls server-side, rotate the exposed key
2Missing server-side authorizationThe UI hides other users' records, but /api/orders/123 returns anyone's order (IDOR)Check ownership on every endpoint
3Database row-level security offSupabase/Firebase tables readable with the public anon keyEnable RLS and write policies per table
4Permissive CORSAccess-Control-Allow-Origin reflects any origin with credentialsExplicit origin allow-list
5InjectionSQL built with string concatenation, eval on user inputParameterised queries, no eval
6Unsafe HTML renderinginnerHTML / dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user contentFramework escaping, a sanitiser, a CSP
7Hallucinated or outdated packagesA suggested dependency that does not exist (or is a typo-squat), or a 2019 versionVerify every new package, enable dependency alerts
8No rate limitingLogin, sign-up, AI and email endpoints callable thousands of times a minutePer-IP and per-account limits
9Verbose errorsStack traces and SQL errors returned to the browserGlobal error handler, generic messages
10Weak session handlingJWTs in localStorage, no expiry, cookies without Secure/HttpOnlyShort-lived tokens, secure cookies
11Unrestricted file uploadAny file type and size, stored in a public bucket under its original nameType and size checks, random names, private storage
12Missing security headersNo HSTS, CSP, frame or nosniff headers on the deployed siteAdd at the host or CDN

Why AI tools make these mistakes

  • They solve the prompt you wrote. "Show the user their orders" gets a filtered UI query, not an authorization rule, unless you ask for one.
  • They learned from public code, including tutorials that skip security for brevity.
  • They lack the full picture. A model editing one file cannot see that another endpoint exposes the same data.
  • They suggest packages from memory, which may be outdated or not exist at all. Attackers now register commonly hallucinated package names ("slopsquatting").

The pre-launch checklist

  1. Search the built front-end bundle for sk-, key, secret, service_role and password. Anything found is already public, so rotate it.
  2. For every API route, write down who may call it and which records they may touch, then test it with a second user account.
  3. Turn on row-level security and run your app as an anonymous user against the database API.
  4. Run npm audit / pip-audit / dotnet list package --vulnerable and open each new dependency's registry page to confirm it is the real one.
  5. Add rate limits to authentication, AI, email and payment endpoints.
  6. Remove debug output and check that errors return generic messages.
  7. Scan the deployed site with the free ZetsApp Website Security Audit for HTTPS, headers, cookies, CORS and vulnerable libraries, and fix everything marked failed.
  8. Ask the AI to review its own code with a security-focused prompt and have a human read the auth and data-access code. Use both, not either.

Prompts that produce safer code

Add standing instructions to your AI tool's project rules:

- Every API endpoint must verify the caller is authenticated AND owns the requested record.
- Never put secrets in client-side code; read them from server environment variables.
- Use parameterised queries only; never build SQL with string concatenation.
- Never use eval, new Function or innerHTML with user input.
- Only use well-known, maintained packages; state the exact version.
- Add rate limiting to auth and any endpoint that sends email, SMS or calls a paid API.

When to bring in engineers

A vibe-coded prototype is a great way to validate an idea. Before it handles payments, health data, children's data or business-critical records, it needs a proper security review and usually some re-architecture. ZetsApp turns prototypes into production systems through MVP development and custom software development, with security review included. See also our guide to the OWASP Top 10:2025.

Frequently asked questions

Is vibe coding secure?

It can be, but not by default. AI coding tools reliably produce working features and frequently miss server-side authorization, secret handling, rate limiting and secure configuration. A structured review before launch closes most of the gaps.

What is the biggest security risk in AI-generated code?

Missing server-side authorization (insecure direct object references) and secrets exposed in client code are the most common serious issues, because the app appears to work correctly in normal use.

What is slopsquatting?

An attack where criminals publish malicious packages under names that AI models commonly hallucinate, so developers who install a suggested dependency without checking it pull in malware.

How do I security-test an app built with Lovable, Bolt or Cursor?

Search the client bundle for secrets, test every API with a second user account, enable database row-level security, audit dependencies, add rate limits, and scan the deployed site's headers, TLS and cookies with a tool like the ZetsApp Website Security Audit.
